title: Meta publishes the Agents Rule of Two for limiting prompt-injection damage
summary: On 31 October 2025 Meta published the Agents Rule of Two, a design rule stating that, until prompt injection can be reliably detected and refused, an agent should satisfy no more than two of three properties within a session: processing untrustworthy inputs, access to sensitive systems or private data, and the ability to change state or communicate externally. When a task needs all three without starting a fresh session, Meta says the agent should not operate autonomously and needs at minimum supervision such as human-in-the-loop approval or another reliable means of validation; the rule is credited to Chromium's rule-of-2 policy and Simon Willison's lethal trifecta.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17. Page title 'Agents Rule of Two: A Practical Approach to AI Agent Security', date 'October 31, 2025', the three properties, the no-more-than-two condition, and the human-in-the-loop requirement all confirmed from the page body. No individual author is named; publisher is Meta via ai.meta.com. The page gives no quantitative figures.
